source.dataset: Spratt and Lisiecki 2016 global sea-level stack

decision.interpretation: The 0.79-0.47 Ma orientation branch is not embedded in an unusually volatile global sea-level interval relative to same-duration windows in the 0-798 ka stack. This weakens a simple high-sea-level-volatility trigger for this local event, while leaving local connectivity scenarios unresolved because no bathymetric/geological threshold is imposed.
decision.role: range-reorganization exposure context only; not a selective-pressure test

claim_boundary: global sea level is not a local Ryukyu/Taiwan connectivity model
sea-level variability is an exposure-opportunity context, not a selective agent
overlapping duration-matched windows are a descriptive temporal reference, not independent replicates
one dated orientation branch cannot identify a general distribution-trigger mechanism
